LOCAL-1.title: Basket: a customer can read another customer's basket by its id
LOCAL-1.body:
**What happens:** a signed-in customer can read another customer's basket by its id. `GET
/rest/basket/<id>` answers `200` with the other customer's products, and the basket page shows them
when the session storage holds that id.

**What should happen:** a customer sees only their own basket (contract rule REQ-BASKET-09,
`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/basket.md`); another customer's id is refused.

**Steps** (accounts created for the run):
1. Customer A signs in and adds Apple Juice (1000ml) to basket `<A_BASKET_ID>`.
2. Customer B signs in at `<base_url>` and sends `GET <base_url>/rest/basket/<A_BASKET_ID>` with B's
   token: `200`, `UserId` of A, A's products.
3. In B's browser session, set session storage `bid` to `<A_BASKET_ID>` and open
   `<base_url>/#/basket`: the table lists A's Apple Juice, "Total Price: 1.99¤".

**Seen:** twice, 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container).

**Note:** Juice Shop is insecure on purpose; this is one of its training vulnerabilities. It is
filed so the case of REQ-BASKET-09 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-2.title: Search: the search term is rendered as markup
LOCAL-2.body: **What happens:** the search term is put into the page as markup. Opening `/#/search?q=%3Cb%3Ebold%3C%2Fb%3E` shows "Search Results - bold", and the title holds a `` element made from the term. **What should happen:** the term is shown back as text (contract rule REQ-SEARCH-04, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/search.md`): "Search Results - ``bold", with no element created. **Seen:** 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container), through the URL alone. Only harmless markup was tried; whether a script runs was not tested. **Severity proposal:** S2 as confirmed (markup injection). Script execution through it would make it S1, since the session token sits in local storage. **Note:** Juice Shop is insecure on purpose; this is one of its training vulnerabilities. It is filed so the case of REQ-SEARCH-04 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-3.title: Basket: /#/basket opens without a session instead of sending to the login
LOCAL-3.body:
**What happens:** `<base_url>/#/basket` opens without a session. The page shows "Your Basket
(anonymous)", an empty table, "Total Price: 0¤" and a disabled Checkout. It asks the server for no
basket and does not send the visitor to the login.

**What should happen:** without a session the basket is not shown; the visitor is sent to the login
(contract rule REQ-BASKET-10, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/basket.md`; decided by the owner,
2026-10-25).

**Seen:** 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium at 1280 px and 412 px, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container),
in a fresh context with the banner and language cookies only.

**Impact:** no data is exposed (no basket request is made); a protected route answers without a
session.

LOCAL-4.title: Sign-up: the password counter reads /20 while the field takes 40 characters
LOCAL-4.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/register` the counter under the password field reads `0/20`,
while the field takes up to 40 characters (`maxlength=40`) and its hint says "Password must be
5-40 characters long.". The counter under "Repeat Password" reads `0/40`.

**What should happen:** the counter shows the same limit as the field and its hint, `/40`
(contract rule REQ-SIGNUP-03, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/signup.md`, gap G1).

**Seen:** 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container), on the empty form; the
app map records `maxlength=40` on the field.

**Severity proposal:** S3: a wrong message with a way around it (the field and the hint say 40).

**Cases:** TC-SIGNUP-19 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-5.title: Search: the title of the product list is not a heading
LOCAL-5.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/search` the title of the list, "All Products" or
"Search Results - `<term>`", is plain text, not a heading. The page has no heading at all, so a
screen reader user cannot jump to the list or learn what it holds from the headings.

**What should happen:** the title is a heading (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1, level A; the a11y row of the
quality dimensions in `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/search.md`, gap G2). The login and basket pages
have a level-1 heading.

**Seen:** 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium and 412 px wide, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container), in the
accessibility tree of the page; the app map records no heading on the route.

**Severity proposal:** S2: a WCAG A failure on a main path, for screen reader users.

**Cases:** TC-SEARCH-22 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-6.title: Toolbar: the search box has no accessible name
LOCAL-6.body:
**What happens:** the toolbar's search box, shown by "Open search", has no accessible name: the
accessibility tree has a `textbox` with no name, on every route, since the toolbar is on every page.

**What should happen:** the box has a name that says what it is for, such as "Search" (WCAG 2.1
SC 4.1.2 and 1.3.1, level A; `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/search.md`, gap G3).

**Seen:** 2026-10-25, desktop Chromium, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container), after pressing "Open
search" on `<base_url>/#/search`; the app map records the textbox without a name.

**Severity proposal:** S2: a WCAG A failure on the main way into search, for screen reader and
voice control users.

**Cases:** TC-SEARCH-23 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-7.title: Checkout: an order is placed without an address, a delivery method or a payment
LOCAL-7.body:
**What happens:** an order is placed without an address, a delivery method or a payment. With a
product in the basket, opening `<base_url>/#/order-summary` directly shows the product, "Delivery
0.00¤" and an enabled "Place your order and pay"; pressing it opens the completion page, and the
order history holds an order with `addressId` and `paymentId` null, `deliveryPrice` 0 and `eta` "5".

**What should happen:** an order needs an address, a delivery method and a payment; placing one
without them is refused (contract rule REQ-CHECKOUT-11, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`).

**Steps** (an account created for the run):
1. Sign in at `<base_url>` and put a product into the basket (`POST <base_url>/api/BasketItems/`).
2. Without choosing an address, a delivery method or a card, open `<base_url>/#/order-summary`. The
   page asks for `/api/Addresss/null`, `/api/Deliverys/null` and `/api/Cards/null` (`400` each).
3. Press "Place your order and pay": `POST <base_url>/rest/basket/<bid>/checkout` answers `200` and the
   page moves to `/#/order-completion/<ORDER_ID>`.
4. `GET <base_url>/rest/order-history` lists the order with no address and no payment.

**Seen:** twice with two accounts, 2026-10-26, desktop Chromium 1280 px, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local
container), through a throwaway script approved at intake.

LOCAL-8.title: Checkout: anyone with an order id reads the order without a session
LOCAL-8.body:
**What happens:** anyone who has an order's id reads the order without a session.
`GET <base_url>/rest/track-order/<ORDER_ID>` answers `200` with the order's products, quantities,
prices, total, delivery price, address and payment ids and the customer's email with its vowels
starred; the tracking page `<base_url>/#/track-result/new?id=<ORDER_ID>` shows the products and the
expected delivery.

**What should happen:** an order's details are shown only to the customer who placed it (contract
rule REQ-CHECKOUT-15, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`; the owner's decision at the
checkout intake, 2026-10-26).

**Steps** (an account created for the run):
1. Sign in at `<base_url>` and place an order; note the id in `/#/order-completion/<ORDER_ID>`.
2. Without any session, send `GET <base_url>/rest/track-order/<ORDER_ID>`.

**Seen:** twice with two orders of two accounts, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container).

**Severity proposal:** S2, agreed with the owner. The id is long and random and the email is
starred, so the order is exposed only to someone who already holds its id; a way to leak or
enumerate ids would make it S1.

LOCAL-9.title: Checkout: the radios of the address, delivery and card tables have no accessible name
LOCAL-9.body:
**What happens:** the radio buttons that choose an address (`<base_url>/#/address/select`), a
delivery method (`/#/delivery-method`) and a card (`/#/payment/shop`) have no accessible name, so a
screen reader announces "radio button" with nothing to tell the rows apart. The header rows of the
same tables have empty cells: the delivery table names only "Price" and "Expected Delivery", the
address and card tables name no column.

**What should happen:** every control has an accessible name (WCAG 2.1 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value, level
A; 1.3.1 Info and Relationships for the headers). The contract's accessibility dimension expects
named radios (`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, G4).

**Steps:** sign in at `<base_url>`, put a product into the basket and check out; read the
accessibility tree of each step: `row "One Day Delivery 0.99¤ 1 Days"` holds `cell > radio` with no
name, and likewise for each address and card row.

**Seen:** 2026-10-26, Chromium 1280 and 412 px, four walks, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the
app map of 2026-10-26 lists `radio "" x3` on `/#/delivery-method`.

LOCAL-10.title: Checkout: the step buttons are named differently from their text, and two name the wrong step
LOCAL-10.body:
**What happens:** the checkout's step buttons have accessible names that differ from the text they
show, and two of them name the wrong step:

| Route | Shows | Accessible name | Leads to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/#/address/select` | Continue | Proceed to payment selection | `/#/delivery-method` |
| `/#/delivery-method` | Continue | Proceed to delivery method selection | `/#/payment/shop` |
| `/#/payment/shop` | Continue | Proceed to review | `/#/order-summary` |
| `/#/order-summary` | Place your order and pay | Complete your purchase | `/#/order-completion/<ORDER_ID>` |

A speech-input user who says "click Continue" reaches none of them, and a screen-reader user hears a
step that is not the next one.

**What should happen:** the accessible name contains the visible text (WCAG 2.1 2.5.3 Label in Name,
level A) and names where the button leads (`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, G5).

**Steps:** sign in at `<base_url>`, put a product into the basket, check out, and read the
accessibility tree of each step.

**Seen:** 2026-10-26, Chromium 1280 and 412 px, four walks, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container).

LOCAL-11.title: Checkout: the order summary and the order history have no heading for their content
LOCAL-11.body:
**What happens:** "Order Summary" on `<base_url>/#/order-summary` and "Order History" on
`<base_url>/#/order-history` are plain text, not headings. The summary's only heading is "Your Basket
(`<EMAIL>`)"; the history page has no heading at all, so heading navigation finds nothing on it.

**What should happen:** each section's title is a heading (WCAG 2.1 1.3.1 Info and Relationships,
level A; 2.4.6 Headings and Labels, AA), as the contract's accessibility dimension expects
(`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, G6). LOCAL-5 is the same pattern on the search list.

**Steps:** sign in at `<base_url>`, place an order, and read the accessibility tree of
`/#/order-summary` before placing it and of `/#/order-history` after.

**Seen:** 2026-10-26, Chromium 1280 and 412 px, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container).

LOCAL-12.title: Checkout: an address without a State shows an empty slot
LOCAL-12.body:
**What happens:** an address saved without a State (an optional field) is shown with an empty slot,
", ,": "1 Probe Street, Probe City, , 10001" on `<base_url>/#/address/select`, the delivery step, the
order summary and the completion page.

**What should happen:** an empty optional part is left out of the line
(`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, G7).

**Steps:** sign in at `<base_url>`, add an address leaving State empty, and look at it on the address
list.

**Seen:** 2026-10-26, Chromium 1280 and 412 px, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container).

LOCAL-13.title: Checkout: the summary and the completion page show 0.00 amounts and raw template text before their answers
LOCAL-13.body:
**What happens:** before their answers arrive, `<base_url>/#/order-summary` shows an empty products
table with Items, Delivery, Promotion and Total Price at 0.00¤, and the completion page
`/#/order-completion/<ORDER_ID>` shows 0.00¤ amounts and the raw template text "You have gained
{{bonus}} Bonus Points from this order!". A customer about to pay sees a total of zero for a moment.

**What should happen:** a loading state, or nothing, until the amounts are known; never a wrong amount
or template text (the contract's perceived-performance dimension,
`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, G8).

**Steps:** sign in at `<base_url>`, go through the checkout and read the summary and the completion
page as soon as their heading appears.

**Seen:** 2026-10-26, Chromium 1280 and 412 px, in the first walk at each width, Juice Shop 20.3.0
(local container); later reads of the same pages show the right amounts.
comments:
**A second form of the same gap** (TC-CHECKOUT-22 runs, 2026-10-26, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation).

With a paid delivery method, the summary's Total Price while the basket's answer is held is the delivery price alone, not 0.00¤: with Fast Delivery it read 0.50¤ for a basket worth more. So the page shows a wrong, non-zero total for a moment, which a customer is even less likely to recognise as a loading state than 0.00¤. TC-CHECKOUT-22 uses Standard Delivery (0.00¤), so its check of a 0.00¤ total does not cover this form; the fix this issue asks for, no amount until the data has arrived, covers both.
**The basket page has the same gap** (TC-BASKET-17 runs, 2026-10-26, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, every run).

While `GET /rest/basket/<bid>` is held (the real answer delayed, not mocked), `<base_url>/#/basket` shows the empty state of REQ-BASKET-02 as if it were the basket's content: "Total Price: 0¤" and "You will gain 0 Bonus Points from this order!", with no loading indicator, until the answer arrives and the products appear. The fix this issue asks for, no amount until the data has arrived, covers the basket page too; TC-BASKET-17 runs as a known gap with this key.

LOCAL-14.title: Checkout: the address form refuses mobile numbers from 1000000 to 1111110, which its message allows
LOCAL-14.body:
**What happens:** the new address form refuses a Mobile Number of 1000000, the lower end of the range its own message gives. Typing 1000000 marks the field invalid, shows "Mobile number must match 1000000-9999999999 format." and keeps Submit disabled. Every value from 1000000 to 1111110 that was tried is refused (1000000, 1000001, 1000010, 1100000, 1111110); 1111111 and above are accepted, up to 9999999999.

**What should happen:** a mobile number from 1000000 to 9999999999 is accepted, as the message states (contract rule REQ-CHECKOUT-03, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`).

**Steps:**
1. Sign in at `<base_url>`, open `<base_url>/#/address/create`.
2. Type 1000000 into Mobile Number and leave the field: the format message shows and Submit stays disabled.
3. Type 1111111: the message goes away.

**Seen:** in every run of TC-CHECKOUT-06 (`apps/juice-shop/specs/checkout/address.spec.ts`), desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). What the server accepts was not checked.

LOCAL-15.title: Checkout: a failed address save empties the form without saying it failed
LOCAL-15.body:
**What happens:** when saving a new address fails, the form empties every field and stays on `<base_url>/#/address/create` without a word: no error message, no notification. Everything the customer typed is lost, and nothing tells them the address was not saved.

**What should happen:** a failed save keeps what was typed and says that it failed, so the customer can try again (the contract records the observed behaviour as a candidate defect: `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`, States, "an address save fails"; REQ-CHECKOUT-04 covers the successful save).

**Steps:** with the address save answering an error (TC-CHECKOUT-23 answers `500` to `POST /api/Addresss/` through `addressSaveFails` in `apps/juice-shop/mocks/checkout-mocks.ts`):
1. Sign in at `<base_url>`, open `<base_url>/#/address/create` and fill every field.
2. Press Submit: the fields empty, no message appears, and the address is not listed on `/#/address/select`.

**Seen:** in every run of TC-CHECKOUT-23, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). The error was produced by a mock; a real server error was not observed.

LOCAL-16.title: Checkout: on a phone the Print icon covers Track Your Order in the order history
LOCAL-16.body:
**What happens:** on a phone, "Track Your Order" on `<base_url>/#/order-history` cannot be pressed: the icon of the "Print order confirmation" button next to it covers it. A click or tap on the button's centre lands on the Print icon (Playwright: "`<mat-icon>note</mat-icon>` from `<div class="col col-5 align-end">` subtree intercepts pointer events"). At 1280 px wide the button works.

**What should happen:** the history's tracking is reachable on every device (contract rule REQ-CHECKOUT-10; the contract's responsive expectation that every step shows the same elements, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/checkout.md`).

**Steps:**
1. Place an order with an account of your own at `<base_url>`.
2. Open `<base_url>/#/order-history` at a phone's width (Pixel 5 emulation, 393 px).
3. Tap "Track Your Order": the Print icon takes the tap.

**Seen:** in a TC-CHECKOUT-14 run (mobile-chrome, trace) and twice in an isolated reproduction with an account and order of its own, Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same reproduction at 1280 px could press it. The completion page's "Track Orders" link still works on a phone.

LOCAL-17.title: Basket: a failed basket answer is shown as an empty basket
LOCAL-17.body:
**What happens:** when the basket's answer fails, `<base_url>/#/basket` shows an ordinary empty basket: the customer's title, a table with only its header row, "Total Price: 0¤", "You will gain 0 Bonus Points from this order!" and a disabled Checkout. No message says the basket could not be loaded, so a customer whose basket holds products is told it is empty.

**What should happen:** a basket that could not be loaded is not shown as an empty one; the page says it failed (contract rule REQ-BASKET-02 describes the empty state; the registry note of TC-BASKET-18 names an ordinary empty basket on an error as a defect; `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/basket.md`).

**Steps** (the error produced by a mock: `basketFails` in `apps/juice-shop/mocks/shop-mocks.ts` answers `500` to `GET /rest/basket/<bid>`):
1. Sign in at `<base_url>` with an account whose basket holds a product.
2. Open `<base_url>/#/basket` while the basket's answer fails.

**Seen:** in every run of TC-BASKET-18, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). A real server error was not observed.

LOCAL-18.title: Search: the page never says Searching for products while the catalogue loads
LOCAL-18.body:
**What happens:** while the product search's answer is pending, `<base_url>/#/search` never says "Searching for products". It shows "All Products", an empty grid and the paginator at "0 of 0" with Previous and Next disabled, so a slow catalogue looks like an empty shop.

**What should happen:** while the products load, the page says "Searching for products" (contract rule REQ-SEARCH-09, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/search.md`; the application's own text `SEARCH_PROCESSING`).

**Steps:** hold the answer to `GET <base_url>/rest/products/search?q=` for a few seconds (TC-SEARCH-14 does it with `slowSearch`, which delays the real answer and lets it through), and open `<base_url>/#/search`.

**Seen:** in the runs of TC-SEARCH-14, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the trace times show the check ran while the answer was held.

LOCAL-19.title: Login: a server error shows the alert [object Object] (unconfirmed)
LOCAL-19.body:
**What happens:** when the login answers a server error, `<base_url>/#/login` shows an alert whose whole text is "[object Object]". The visitor stays on the form without a session, but the message says nothing a person can act on.

**What should happen:** a server error on the login keeps the visitor on `/#/login` with a message (TC-LOGIN-15 and the contract's states, `apps/juice-shop/docs/features/login.md`; REQ-LOGIN-02 for the refusal's alert). Which words the message should use is for the contract owner.

**Steps** (the error produced by a mock: `loginFails` in `apps/juice-shop/mocks/account-mocks.ts` answers `500` with the JSON body `{ "error": "status 500" }`):
1. Open `<base_url>/#/login`, fill an email and a password, press Log in.
2. The alert reads "[object Object]".

**Seen:** in the runs of TC-LOGIN-15, desktop Chromium and Pixel 5 emulation, 2026-10-26, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). The body comes from the mock; a real server error's body was not observed, so it may render differently.

**Severity proposal:** S3 (a wrong message with a way around: trying again).

LOCAL-20.title: Contact: the feedback form's rating slider has no accessible name
LOCAL-20.body:
**What happens:** the star rating of the feedback form on `<base_url>/#/contact` is a slider whose input has no accessible name (axe `label`), so a screen reader announces an unnamed slider.

**What should happen:** the slider is named after what it rates, such as "Rating" (WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2 and 1.3.1, level A).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S3: the form can still be sent, but screen reader users do not know what the slider sets.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key.

LOCAL-21.title: About Us: the feedback carousel's images have no alternative text and the carousel cannot be reached with the keyboard
LOCAL-21.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/about` the customer feedback carousel shows images with no alternative text (axe `image-alt`, every slide: 4 on desktop, 8 on mobile), and its scrolling region cannot be reached with the keyboard (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`).

**What should happen:** each image has an alternative text with what it shows, or is marked decorative when the slide's text says it all, and the carousel can be reached and moved with the keyboard (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.1.1 and 2.1.1, level A).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S2: the carousel's content is lost to screen reader users and out of reach for keyboard users.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key for both rules.

LOCAL-22.title: About Us: a link in the text is told apart by colour alone
LOCAL-22.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/about` a link inside the paragraph text (the one to `legal.md`) is told apart from the text around it by colour alone (axe `link-in-text-block`, desktop).

**What should happen:** the link has a mark besides colour, such as an underline, or enough contrast with the text around it (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1, level A).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S3: users who do not see the colour difference can miss the link; it is still reachable with the keyboard.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key.

LOCAL-23.title: Basket and order summary: the products table's header row has no column headers
LOCAL-23.body:
**What happens:** the products table of `<base_url>/#/basket` and `<base_url>/#/order-summary` has a header row whose children are not the column headers the row role requires (axe `aria-required-children` on `mat-header-row`), so a screen reader cannot pair the cells with their columns reliably.

**What should happen:** the header row holds column headers, as a table's header row must (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.3.1 and 4.1.2, level A).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S3: the rows still read in order; only the column relation is lost.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key; TC-BASKET-21 compares against the same baseline.

LOCAL-24.title: Basket and order summary: the email in the title has too little contrast
LOCAL-24.body:
**What happens:** the email in the basket's title, "Your Basket (`<EMAIL>`)", on `<base_url>/#/basket` and `<base_url>/#/order-summary`, has a contrast ratio below 4.5:1 against its background (axe `color-contrast`).

**What should happen:** text of that size has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3, level AA).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S3: the email is hard to read for users with low vision; it is also in the account menu.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key.

LOCAL-25.title: Search: the stock ribbon of a product card has too little contrast
LOCAL-25.body:
**What happens:** the stock ribbon of a product card ("Only `<n>` left"), on `<base_url>/#/` and `<base_url>/#/search`, has a contrast ratio below 4.5:1 (axe `color-contrast`, desktop). The ribbon shows only for products with little stock, which changes with each start of the shop.

**What should happen:** the ribbon's text has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.3, level AA).

**Seen:** 2026-10-29, the a11y sweep (`npm run lanes:a11y`, axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa) on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container); the same in two consecutive runs. The axe result is attached to each sweep test of the route.

**Severity proposal:** S3: the stock warning is hard to read for users with low vision; adding to the basket still works.

**Cases:** the a11y sweep's baseline (`apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json`) cites this key for every route.

LOCAL-26.title: Every page: keyboard focus is not visible on any control
LOCAL-26.body:
**What happens:** no control shows where the keyboard focus is. On the login form (Username,
Password, Login), the product list ("Add to cart", the sort) and the cart ("Remove", "Checkout"),
a control reached with Tab is drawn exactly as before: same computed style (`outline-style: none`,
no `box-shadow`, same border and background) and the same pixels, while `:focus-visible` is true.

**What should happen:** a keyboard user sees which control has focus (login contract rule
REQ-LOGIN-09, `apps/saucedemo/docs/features/login.md`, gap G2; WCAG 2.1 SC 2.4.7, level AA).

**Steps:**
1. Open `<base_url>/` and press Tab: focus moves to Username, but nothing on the page changes.
2. Press Tab twice more to reach Login: still nothing marks it.
3. Signed in, open `<base_url>/inventory.html` and `<base_url>/cart.html` and Tab through: same.

**Devices:** desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome (Pixel 7 emulation).

**Evidence:** TC-LOGIN-09 fails on both projects, 4 of 4 runs, 2026-10-31 (trace and screenshot in
the local run's `test-results/`); a read-only probe compared the element screenshots and computed
styles before and after focus on the list and the cart, 2026-10-31.

LOCAL-27.title: Every page but the login: a page opened directly is answered 404
LOCAL-27.body:
**What happens:** every page but the login answers `404` to a direct request for its document.
`/inventory.html`, `/inventory-item.html?id=4`, `/cart.html` and `/checkout-step-one.html` all
return `404 Not Found`, and the browser then draws the page from the script, so the user sees it.
Only `/` answers `200`.

**What should happen:** a page that exists is answered `200` (product list contract,
`apps/saucedemo/docs/features/inventory.md`, gap G1). A monitor, a crawler or a link checker now
reports these pages as missing.

**Steps:**
1. Request `<base_url>/inventory.html` (a reload, a bookmark or a plain GET): the status is `404`.
2. Repeat for `/inventory-item.html?id=4`, `/cart.html`, `/checkout-step-one.html`: `404` each.
3. Request `<base_url>/`: `200`.

**Devices:** any; seen on desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome (Pixel 7 emulation), and on a plain
HTTP GET.

**Evidence:** TC-INVENTORY-15 fails on both projects, 4 of 4 runs, 2026-10-31 (the document's
status is 404); a read-only probe requested the five routes, 2026-10-31.

LOCAL-28.title: Reset App State: the open cart and product list keep showing the products until a reload
LOCAL-28.body:
**What happens:** "Reset App State" empties the cart in the browser's storage and removes the cart
badge, but the page that is open keeps showing the old cart. On the cart page both products are
still listed with their "Remove" buttons; on the product list their buttons still read "Remove".
A reload shows the empty cart.

**What should happen:** the reset empties the cart, so the badge disappears and the cart lists
nothing (cart contract rule REQ-CART-08, `apps/saucedemo/docs/features/cart.md`).

**Steps:**
1. Signed in, with Sauce Labs Backpack and Sauce Labs Bike Light in the cart, open
   `<base_url>/cart.html`: 2 rows, badge 2.
2. Open the menu and choose "Reset App State": the badge disappears, the 2 rows stay.
3. Reload: the cart lists nothing.
4. Same on `<base_url>/inventory.html`: after the reset both products still show "Remove" until a
   reload.

**Devices:** desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome (Pixel 7 emulation).

**Evidence:** TC-CART-10 fails on both projects, 4 of 4 runs, 2026-10-31 (2 rows after the reset);
a read-only probe recorded badge, rows, "Remove" buttons and storage before the reset, after it and
after a reload, on both pages and both devices, 2026-10-31.

LOCAL-29.title: Logout leaves the cart for whoever signs in next on the same browser
LOCAL-29.body:
**What happens:** Logout ends the session but leaves the cart in the browser. Whoever signs in
next on the same browser, with any account, finds the previous user's products in the cart. The
cart lives in local storage (`cart-contents`), and Logout removes only the session cookie.

**What should happen:** after Logout and a new sign-in the cart is empty, so a shared browser does
not show one user's cart to the next (cart contract gap G3 and login gap G5,
`apps/saucedemo/docs/features/cart.md` and `login.md`; registry case TC-CART-12).

**Steps:**
1. Signed in as `<USER_A>`, add Sauce Labs Backpack to the cart: badge 1.
2. Open the menu and choose Logout: the login page shows.
3. Sign in again on the same browser (as `<USER_A>` or another account): the badge shows 1 and the
   cart lists Sauce Labs Backpack.

**Devices:** desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome (Pixel 7 emulation).

**Severity:** S2. The data is another user's cart, exposed only on the same browser; it holds no
personal data.

**Evidence:** TC-CART-12 fails on both projects, 4 of 4 runs, 2026-10-31, at the empty-cart check
after the new sign-in (trace in the local run's `test-results/`).

LOCAL-30.title: Cart: the cart button is named "Cart, 1 items" with one product
LOCAL-30.body:
**What happens:** with one product in the cart, the cart button's accessible name is
"Cart, 1 items", so a screen reader announces "1 items".

**What should happen:** "Cart, 1 item" for one product, "Cart, `<n>` items" for more and
"Cart, empty" for none (cart contract gap G1, `apps/saucedemo/docs/features/cart.md`; registry case
TC-CART-15).

**Steps:**
1. Signed in, add one product to the cart on `<base_url>/inventory.html`.
2. Read the accessible name of the cart button in the header (the accessibility tree, or a screen
   reader): "Cart, 1 items".

**Devices:** desktop Chromium and mobile Chrome (Pixel 7 emulation).

**Evidence:** TC-CART-15 fails on both projects, 4 of 4 runs, 2026-10-31, at the one-product name;
the empty and two-product names are as expected.

LOCAL-31.title: Juice Shop: documents carry no Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy
LOCAL-31.body:
**What happens:** the documents Juice Shop serves carry no Content-Security-Policy, no
Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy header. They send `Feature-Policy: payment 'self'`, the
retired name of Permissions-Policy, and no Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy. X-Content-Type-Options
(`nosniff`) and X-Frame-Options (`SAMEORIGIN`) are present.

**What should happen:** every document carries a Content-Security-Policy, a Referrer-Policy that
keeps the path from other origins (`strict-origin-when-cross-origin` or stricter) and a
Permissions-Policy in place of Feature-Policy.

**Steps:**
1. Request `<base_url>/` and read the response headers (the browser's network panel, or any HTTP
   client).
2. The headers above are missing; `Feature-Policy` is there instead of `Permissions-Policy`.

**Devices:** any; the headers come from the server, desktop Chromium and the ZAP baseline scan both
show them.

**Severity:** S3. Juice Shop is insecure on purpose; the missing policies widen what its injection
defects (LOCAL-2) can do, and change nothing a user sees.

**Evidence:** the security headers sweep (`apps/juice-shop/specs/security/headers.spec.ts`) fails on
`/` anonymous and signed in with an empty baseline, 2026-11-03; the ZAP baseline lane reports
plugins 10038 (CSP header not set), 10063 (deprecated Feature Policy header) and 90004
(Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy missing) on the same documents.

LOCAL-32.title: Juice Shop: every response allows any origin (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *)
LOCAL-32.body:
**What happens:** every response of Juice Shop, documents, scripts and REST answers alike, carries
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so any site's scripts may read what the shop answers to a request
that carries no credentials.

**What should happen:** the shop names the origins it trusts, or sends no CORS header on responses
no other origin needs.

**Steps:**
1. Request `<base_url>/` or `<base_url>/rest/admin/application-version` and read the response
   headers.
2. `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` is present on both.

**Devices:** any; the header comes from the server.

**Severity:** S3. The wildcard does not apply to requests with cookies, and the shop's REST API
authenticates with a bearer token, so a page of another site reads only what an anonymous client
already could.

**Evidence:** the ZAP baseline lane reports plugin 10098 (Cross-Domain Misconfiguration) on the
documents and scripts it fetched, 2026-11-03.

LOCAL-33.title: Swag Labs: documents carry none of the security headers, Strict-Transport-Security included
LOCAL-33.body:
**What happens:** the documents of Swag Labs carry none of the security headers: no
Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no X-Content-Type-Options, no
Referrer-Policy, no Permissions-Policy, and no Strict-Transport-Security although the site is served
over https. Any site can frame the login page.

**What should happen:** every document carries those headers, with Strict-Transport-Security on
https and a framing policy (`frame-ancestors` or `X-Frame-Options: DENY`) on the login page at least.

**Steps:**
1. Request `<base_url>/` and read the response headers.
2. None of the headers above is present; the same holds for `<base_url>/inventory.html` and the
   other pages of the shop.

**Devices:** any; the headers come from the host.

**Severity:** S3. A public demonstration shop without real accounts; the missing framing policy is
the one a user could be tricked through.

**Evidence:** the security headers sweep (`apps/saucedemo/specs/security/headers.spec.ts`) fails on
`/` with six gaps and an empty baseline, 2026-11-03, desktop Chromium. Read-only: the sweep opens
pages and reads their answers; the ZAP lane never scans this host.

LOCAL-34.title: Basket: the decrease, increase and remove buttons of a row have no accessible name
LOCAL-34.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/basket` the decrease, increase and remove buttons of each product row have no accessible name (axe `button-name`, three per row), so a screen reader announces "button" with nothing to tell them apart.

**What should happen:** each button says what it does and to which product (WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.2, level A). The basket contract notes it as gap G4 (`apps/juice-shop/docs/features/basket.md`).

**Steps:** sign in, add two products, open `<base_url>/#/basket`, run axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa and wcag21aa: 6 `button-name` violations.

**Seen:** 2026-11-05, the axe scans of TC-CHECKOUT-29, on the six device projects of `QA_ENV=ci`, twice each: 12 of 12 runs, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). The order summary shows the same products without these buttons and has no such violation.

**Severity proposal:** S2: a WCAG A failure on a main path; keyboard and pointer users are not affected, screen reader users must guess which button changes what.

**Cases:** the baseline `apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json` cites this key, which TC-CHECKOUT-29 and TC-BASKET-21 compare against.
comments: **Correction to Cases:** TC-BASKET-21 has no spec yet, so today only TC-CHECKOUT-29 compares against this entry of the baseline. TC-BASKET-21 will when it is automated (JS-08).

LOCAL-35.title: Order completion: the Track Orders link is told apart by colour alone
LOCAL-35.body:
**What happens:** on `<base_url>/#/order-completion/<ORDER_ID>` the Track Orders link inside the confirmation text is told apart from the text around it by colour alone (axe `link-in-text-block`, at `a[routerlink="/track-result/new"]`).

**What should happen:** the link has a mark besides colour, such as an underline, or enough contrast with the text around it (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1, level A).

**Steps:** place an order, then run axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa and wcag21aa on the completion page.

**Seen:** 2026-11-05, the axe scan of TC-CHECKOUT-29, on the six device projects of `QA_ENV=ci`, twice each: 12 of 12 runs, Juice Shop 20.3.0 (local container). LOCAL-22 is the same rule on another page, `/#/about`.

**Severity proposal:** S3: users who do not see the colour difference can miss the link; it is still reachable with the keyboard and from the order history.

**Cases:** the baseline `apps/juice-shop/a11y-known.json` cites this key for every route, since the route holds the order id. TC-CHECKOUT-29 compares against it.
